newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Central Africa CFA cash injections up 34pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Central Africa CFA cash injections up 34pct in Jan.

text.p: Central Bank (BEAC) cash injections into the Central African CFA franc zone rose again in January, fired by a strong demand for liquidity to fund commodity marketing seasons, the bank's monthly bulletin said.

The volume of total transactions on the monetary market increased by 34.3 percent to 23.1 billion CFA from 17.2 billion in December. The volume rose in December after five relatively stable months because of the marketing seasons.

Bank deposits at the BEAC fell again in January but certain banks deposited money at the Central bank to mop up excess liquidity. The average amount deposited for the zone decreased to 64.8 billion CFA, compared to 65.7 billion CFA in December.
"The decrease in bank deposits at the BEAC is mainly due to an increase in demand for credit, which is forcing banks to dip into their reserves," said the bulletin.

Banks in Cameroon retain the highest average daily deposit rate, but this stabilised in January at 32.4 billion CFA, against 32.7 billion CFA in December. Over 70 percent of its deposits can be traced to one bank, which is decreasing its excess liquidity via deposits at the Central Bank.

Banks in the Central African Republic cut their deposits by 50 percent this month, earmarking their reserves for financing the cotton marketing season and a resumption of activity in the oil marketing sector following an army mutiny.
Gabonese banks increased deposits, which reached 23.8 billion CFA, against 21.2 billion in December, due to an inflow of money from petrol companies which created excess liquidity.
Interbank market activity decreased again, from 3.9 billion CFA in December to 2.7 billion in January. Gabon was the only bank to register any operations on the interbank market.
The average interbank rate in January was 5.415 percent, compared to 6.108 percent the previous month.

There was a notable absence of activity in Chad as banks were financing the start of the cotton marketing season, according to an offical from the BEAC. The BEAC money market rates were unchanged with the intervention rate at 9.75 percent and the two to seven day lending rate at 10 percent.
The Central African monetary zone groups six countries in the region -- Cameroon, Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea and Chad.
